list: The official 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze (28 hidden). Names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them, as listed by the public trophy trackers.
note: Every guide below is written in my own words for this guide. Facts about counts, the single-playthrough structure, the lack of mission replay and the one possibly missable trophy come from the cited public guides. Nothing here is copied from another guide.

trophies.guide: This is the Platinum, and there is no shortcut to it: it unlocks by itself the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so your whole job is the other 54. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap below, not as a trophy you chase directly. The public guides put the whole run at roughly 200 hours, and almost all of that time sits in the 100% completion checklist behind A Long Road, so keep that checklist open from early on. Because there is no mission replay and no second playthrough needed, one careful run is enough — just do not leave the one possibly missable meditation (Positive Mental Attitude) until after the story. When the Platinum pops, everything else is already done.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.roadmap_note: Last trophy: it pops automatically once the other 54 are earned.

steps: Follow the six roadmap stages in order, ticking each trophy off in this tracker as it pops.
Check Progress > Stats > 100% Completion regularly so nothing on the A Long Road checklist is left behind.
Leave no trophy for 'later' that depends on a story moment; free roam after the story covers the rest.

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission of the story, so this is one of the first trophies most players will earn, and it cannot be missed — just play the story from the start. It introduces Lucia and Jason and sets up the fishing thread that returns later in Baited My Tackle, so take the opening at a relaxed pace and learn the controls it teaches. There is no special requirement beyond finishing the mission itself: no time limit, no optional objective and no choice that gates it. If you are following this guide from the beginning, tick it off as soon as the mission-complete screen appears and move on to Chapter 1.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: the opening mission, Gone Fishing.

steps: Start a new game and play through the opening until the Gone Fishing mission begins.
Follow the on-screen objectives to the end of the mission.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.

trophies.guide: Chapter 1 is the first full chapter of the story, and this trophy pops when its final mission is complete — story progress alone earns it, so it cannot be missed. The one thing to do inside Chapter 1 that you cannot do later is the missable meditation tied to Positive Mental Attitude: the public guides report a Chapter 1 meditation spot with Lucia, so meditate at every spot you find while the chapter is still open rather than assuming you can return. Otherwise, simply play the chapter's missions in order, and use the time to try side activities as they unlock, since several activity trophies are easier when you meet them early. The chapter trophy is your signal that the opening act is done and the map is opening up.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: finish every mission in Chapter 1.

steps: Play every Chapter 1 mission in order until the chapter closes.

The trophy pops at the end of the chapter's final mission.

trophies.guide: This trophy pops when Chapter 2 is complete, so like the other chapter trophies it is earned by story progress alone and cannot be missed. By Chapter 2 the game's systems are open — partner play, robberies and the wider Leonida map — so use the chapter to bank progress toward the open-world trophies that run alongside the story: discover vehicles for Whip It Good, try activities for Master of None, and keep an eye out for meditation spots. There is no chapter-specific requirement beyond finishing its missions, and free roam continues after the story, so anything you skip here can be picked up later except the Chapter 1 meditation noted under Positive Mental Attitude. Tick it off at the chapter's final mission and keep going.

trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: finish every mission in Chapter 2.

trophies.guide: Chapter 3 closes with this trophy, earned by finishing its missions in order — story progress alone, nothing to miss. By now Vice City itself is the playground, so this is a good chapter to push the exploration trophies: work through the map for The Goodtime State, keep discovering vehicles, and clear Shooting Range challenges and drone races as you pass them rather than leaving them all for the endgame. The heist and robbery missions in this stretch also feed the crime trophies (bank vaults, armored trucks, illegal operations), so attempt those objectives whenever the story hands you the chance. The trophy pops at the chapter's final mission.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: finish every mission in Chapter 3.

trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last numbered chapter, and its trophy pops when its final mission is complete — again, story progress alone, nothing to miss. Before you push into the finale, this is the moment to check the story-linked trophies that are easiest while missions are still flowing: the partner robberies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy), the set-piece moments (Catch Me If You Can, Capital Offense) and any stranger strands you have open, since the guides report no mission replay once a mission is done. Free roam continues after the story, so open-world cleanup is safe to leave, but anything tied to a mission's scripted moment is best done while you are in it. Finish the chapter, tick it off, and head for the final mission.

trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: finish every mission in Chapter 4.

trophies.guide: This gold trophy pops when the final mission is complete, closing the story. It is the only gold trophy that is hidden on PlayStation, which is why the spoiler setting in this guide masks it until you earn it. There is no extra requirement: finish the mission and the trophy is yours, and free roam carries on afterwards, so the end of the story is really the start of the cleanup phase — activities, collectibles, crime sprees and the 100% checklist. Because the public guides report no mission replay, make sure the story-moment trophies are done before you start the finale (see the roadmap's Stage 1 checklist). After the credits, switch to Stage 2 of the roadmap and work the open world.

trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: finish the final mission — the story's end, and the start of free-roam cleanup.

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a story mission, and Trust pops when you complete it — no optional objective, no choice and no time limit beyond the mission itself. Mission trophies like this one are the backbone of the story stage: just play the missions as they come and they stack up on their own. Because the guides report no mission replay, treat each mission trophy as a one-time pass — if a mission also holds a set-piece moment for another trophy (a robbery, a chase, a vehicle trick), do that trophy's step while you are inside the mission rather than assuming a replay. Breakfast Run itself asks nothing extra, so finish it, tick it off, and keep moving through the chapter.
trophies.name: Trust
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: complete the Breakfast Run mission when it appears.

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a story heist mission, and Break the Bank pops when you complete it. Heist missions are usually the longest and most involved in a chapter, so go in prepared: stock up on ammo and armour before you start, since the mission itself is the only requirement and failing and retrying it costs nothing but time. The heist also sets up the robbery thread that continues in the open world — bank vaults for Maximum Withdrawal, armored trucks for A Classic Blitz Play and gang operations for Pest Control — so treat it as a rehearsal for those. Finish the heist, tick the trophy off, and keep the robbery skills warm for the crime stage of the roadmap.

trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: complete The Cartel Heist mission.

trophies.guide: Child's Play is a story mission, and Family Matters pops when you complete it — story progress alone, with no extra objective. Like every mission trophy in this list, the only real advice is to play the missions in order and not to rush past the moments inside them: with no mission replay reported by the public guides, a set-piece moment inside a mission is best attempted while you are playing it. Child's Play itself has no side requirement, so finish the mission, tick it off in the tracker, and continue the chapter. If you are tracking your run, this is one of the six named-mission trophies that sit between the chapter trophies in Stage 1.

trophies.guide: Headliners is a story mission, and DWNFALL pops when you complete it. The name hints at the music and nightlife side of Vice City, and the mission sits among the named story missions that fill out Stage 1 of the roadmap alongside the chapter trophies. There is no extra requirement beyond finishing the mission, so play it through and the trophy follows. As with every mission trophy, the practical advice is the same: play missions in order, and if the mission contains a set-piece you recognise from another trophy's guide — a robbery, a chase, a stunt — attempt that step while you are inside it, since the public guides report no mission replay. Otherwise, finish Headliners and move on.

trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a story mission set around Vice City International Airport, and Hi-Jacked pops when you complete it. Airport missions tend to mix driving, shooting and vehicle set-pieces, so go in with a full loadout and a fast car in mind for the getaway. This mission also pairs naturally with Catch Me If You Can, the trophy for an unscheduled departure at VCIA — if that moment comes during or right after this mission, take it, because the guides report no mission replay. The mission trophy itself asks nothing extra: finish VCIA Takedown and it pops. Tick it off in Stage 1 and keep the airport in mind for the open-world departure trophy.

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a story mission, and Snow Storm pops when you complete it. The name suggests a large, chaotic operation — the kind of mission where preparation pays: full armour, a good weapon set and a sturdy vehicle before you start. Like the other named-mission trophies it asks nothing beyond completion, so the trophy is really a milestone marker for your progress through the story. Play it, finish it, and tick it off in Stage 1. If the operation throws vehicles or combat set-pieces at you, remember the combat trophies running in parallel — Gunslinger (five takedowns in one Combat Focus) and Challenging Tank (Rhino tanks) can both be attempted whenever the mission hands you the right moment.

trophies.guide: This gold trophy is the hardest in the list and the real gate to the Platinum: it requires 100% completion, and the public guides rank it the toughest trophy in the game. Track it in-game under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion, where the checklist shows every remaining objective — story missions, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and challenges all feed into it. The smart way to earn it is to work the checklist from the start rather than leaving it for the end: every trophy in this guide contributes to it, and the roadmap stages are ordered so the checklist shrinks steadily as you play. Expect most of the roughly 200-hour Platinum run to sit here, especially the long grinds — 250 stunts, 100 WAiNK It locations, all Shooting Range golds and full Leonida exploration. Keep cheats off the whole run, since the guides report that using a cheat disables trophies and saving.
trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.roadmap_note: Final stage: finish the in-game 100% checklist (Progress > Stats > 100% Completion).

Work the roadmap stages in order; each stage clears part of the checklist.
When only long grinds remain, clear them one at a time — stunts, WAiNK It, Shooting Range, exploration.

trophies.guide: Stunts are the jumps, near-misses, airtime and driving tricks the game tracks as you drive, and this silver trophy needs 250 of them. The count is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so every jump you land and every close call on the road already counts — you do not need to do them in one session or in one place. The fastest way to farm them is to find a good jump spot, ideally a ramp or a raised road edge with a long landing, and repeat clean jumps in a fast, sturdy car; the game counts each successful stunt, so a reliable loop beats a spectacular one-off. Mix in near-misses in traffic for variety, since those count too, and keep an eye on the counter in the stats screen. Treat it as a background trophy while you travel between missions, then farm the remainder in the cleanup stage.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.roadmap_note: Activities stage: builds up while driving; farm the remainder after the story.

sources.name: GTABase — GTA 6 achievements & trophies list

steps: Drive aggressively but cleanly from the start — jumps, airtime and near-misses all count.
Find a repeatable jump with a long, flat landing and loop it in a fast car.
Check your stunt count in the stats screen and farm the remainder after the story.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Leonida offers nine types of activity, and this trophy pops when you have tried each one at least once — you only need to try them, not win or finish them. The public guides count nine activity types, and the ones the trophy list names include fishing, the Shooting Range, drone racing, other races, arcade games, bowling and meditation, with more to discover as the map opens. The practical approach is to sample each activity the first time you meet it instead of walking past: play one arcade game (Stick Fiddler), fire one round at the Shooting Range, enter one race, fish once, meditate once. Use the tracker to note which types you have tried, since the game does not always make the list obvious. One session of sampling in free roam is enough to pop it.
trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.roadmap_note: Activities stage: sample each of the 9 activity types once.

steps: As each activity unlocks, try it once — fishing, Shooting Range, races, arcade, bowling, meditation and the rest.
Work through the activity list in this guide and tick each type off as you sample it.
The trophy pops when the ninth type is tried.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The Shooting Range holds 42 challenges, and this silver trophy needs a gold medal in every one of them — the purest skill test in the list. Each challenge is a timed shooting trial with a score threshold for gold, so the work is learning each range's layout, weapon and target pattern, then repeating it until your run is clean. Start with the weapons you handle best, use the range's practice runs to learn target order, and take golds in batches rather than grinding one challenge for an hour straight. Steady aim beats fast panic fire: short, controlled bursts and reloads between waves keep your score up. Because there are 42 of them, spread the work across the playthrough and leave the hardest few for the cleanup stage when your aim is warm.
trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.roadmap_note: Activities stage: gold all 42 Shooting Range challenges, a few at a time.

steps: Visit a Shooting Range and learn each challenge's targets, weapon and gold threshold.
Clear the easy golds first, then practise the hard ones in short sessions.
Track your golds in this guide; the trophy pops when all 42 are gold.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at 14 locations across Leonida, and this trophy needs a win at every one of them. Drone racing is a flying skill: learn the course gates, cut corners only where the gates allow it, and keep the drone low and fast rather than climbing for a view. Each location is its own race, so you can clear them one at a time as you travel the map, and a loss costs nothing — just retry the race until you win it. There is no requirement to win them in any order, so clear the locations near your current missions first and mop up the remote ones during exploration. The trophy pops when the fourteenth location is won.
trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.roadmap_note: Activities stage: win a drone race at all 14 Top Fun locations.

steps: Find a Top Fun drone race location and learn its gates on a practice run.

Repeat at all 14 locations; the trophy pops on the last win.

trophies.guide: This trophy needs wins in 20 different races — different events, not the same race twenty times — so variety is the requirement. Leonida's race scene covers street races, off-road events, boat and air races and the Top Fun drone races, and any win counts as long as the event is one you have not already won. The practical route is to enter every race you pass: accept the invitation, learn the route on the first attempt, then win it on the retry, and move on to the next event instead of farming a favourite. Keep a note of which events you have won in this tracker so you do not waste time re-running one. Twenty wins sounds like a lot, but spread across the map's race events it comes naturally during the activities stage.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.roadmap_note: Activities stage: win 20 different race events across Leonida.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is the fishing rival, and this trophy needs you to beat him in a fishing challenge — a head-to-head contest rather than casual fishing. Fishing challenges reward the right spot, the right bait and steady reeling: watch the line tension, reel when the fish runs toward you and ease off when it fights, since a snapped line ends the attempt. Cal's challenge is a duel, so treat it like a race: learn the fishing mechanics in free play first (the opening mission Gone Fishing teaches the basics), then take the challenge when you are comfortable with the reeling rhythm. If you lose, challenge him again — there is no limit on attempts. The trophy pops the moment you out-fish him.

trophies.roadmap_note: Activities stage: beat Cal in a fishing challenge.

steps: Practise fishing in free play until the reeling rhythm feels natural.

Win the challenge; retry as often as needed, the trophy pops on the win.

trophies.guide: Arcades across Leonida hold playable games, and this trophy needs you to complete just one of them — finish a full game, not merely start it. Pick whichever cabinet appeals to you: the classic-style machines are usually the quickest to complete, and the trophy counts completion rather than a high score, so play to finish rather than to chase points. Arcade games also count as one of the nine activity types for Master of None, so this trophy does double duty. If you are short on time, choose the shortest game on the cabinet and see it through to its end screen. The trophy pops when the game completes.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy is one of the stranger characters whose mission strand runs alongside the story, and this trophy pops when you complete his final mission. Stranger strands unlock as you explore and meet their characters, and each strand is a short chain of missions — so the way to this trophy is to find Andy early, then take his missions whenever they appear on the map instead of leaving them for the endgame. The public guides note that stranger missions are not part of the 100% completion checklist, but they are part of Strangers & Freaks, so clearing Andy's strand counts toward both this trophy and that silver. Finish his last mission and the trophy pops; then move on to the next stranger on the list.

Kenton's strand also counts toward the eight strands needed for Strangers & Freaks. Finish his last mission and the trophy is yours.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Strangers & Freaks is the silver trophy for completing eight stranger mission strands — the side-character chains that run alongside the story, including Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and Bret. Each strand is a short series of missions that starts when you meet its character in the open world, and the strands unlock as the story opens new areas, so the work is mostly exploration: roam Leonida, meet everyone marked on the map, and take their missions as they appear. The public guides note that stranger missions are not part of the 100% completion checklist, so they are easy to overlook — keep a list of the strands you have started in this tracker and finish each one before moving on. Eight completed strands pop the silver, and the six named-character trophies in this guide are six of them.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: This is the one trophy the public guides flag as possibly missable, so treat it as the most important trophy in this guide. There are 18 meditation spots across Leonida, and the guides report that one of them is a Chapter 1 moment with Lucia — a balcony meditation early in the story that may not be available later, because the game has no mission replay. The rule is simple: meditate at every spot you find, the moment you find it, and never walk past one assuming you can return. In Chapter 1, take the meditation the story offers you. After that, work the remaining spots during exploration — scenic overlooks, beaches and quiet corners are the usual places — and keep count in this tracker. The trophy pops at the eighteenth spot.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.roadmap_note: Activities stage — but START in Chapter 1: the Lucia meditation may not be repeatable.

steps: In Chapter 1, take the meditation the story offers with Lucia — do not skip it.
After that, meditate at every spot you find, the moment you find it.
Track your count here; the trophy pops at the 18th spot.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret is a stranger whose strand centres on hunting, and Fair Game pops when you hunt a unique animal for him. The unique animal is a one-of-a-kind target — a rare beast in a specific part of Leonida — so the work is tracking it down rather than hunting in general: follow Bret's strand, listen to his directions about where the animal roams, and approach quietly with a scoped rifle or bow rather than charging in. Unique animals usually need a clean, careful shot, so take your time, use cover and crouch, and be ready for the animal to bolt. Finish the hunt, return to Bret, and the trophy pops when the strand's hunting objective is complete.
trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.roadmap_note: Side stage: hunt Bret's unique animal.

Follow his directions to the unique animal's territory.
Hunt it with a careful, quiet approach; the trophy pops when the hunt completes.

trophies.guide: Collectible cards are scattered across Leonida in packs, and this silver trophy needs three complete sets — every card in three sets, not just three cards. Cards turn up in shops, in the open world and as rewards, so the practical approach is to pick up every card you see from the start and keep a set list in this tracker, noting which sets are close to complete. Sets are finished by finding their missing cards, so once a set is one or two cards short, focus your search on the area those cards come from rather than wandering at random. Trading or buying duplicates does not complete a set; only the missing cards do. Three finished sets pop the silver.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.roadmap_note: Collectibles stage: complete 3 full card sets.

steps: Pick up every collectible card you find from the start of the game.
Keep a set list here and note which sets are nearly complete.
Hunt the missing cards for three sets; the silver pops on the third completed set.

trophies.guide: WAiNK It is the in-world photo-sharing activity — you snap and share a shot at a location, and the game counts it — and this silver trophy needs 100 locations. The trick is that it is a volume grind with a simple loop: go somewhere new, open the WAiNK It prompt, take the shot and move on. The fastest route is to fold it into exploration for The Goodtime State: every new area you visit for the map trophy is also a WAiNK It location, so the two trophies progress together. Do not try to farm all 100 in one sitting; instead, WAiNK It everywhere you go from the start, and the count climbs without feeling like a grind. The trophy pops at the hundredth location.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.roadmap_note: Collectibles stage: WAiNK It at 100 locations — fold it into map exploration.

steps: From the start, WAiNK It at every new place you visit.
Fold it into exploration — each new area is a location for both this and The Goodtime State.
The silver pops at the 100th location.

trophies.guide: Challenges are the game's side objectives — small tasks scattered across activities, combat, driving and exploration — and this trophy needs 50 of them completed. The count is cumulative, so anything you complete while playing normally already counts: race wins, stunt milestones, hunting, fishing and more all feed the challenge list. The best approach is to open the challenges menu regularly and pick off the ones that are nearly done, since the list shows your progress on each. Because the trophy only needs 50, and the game holds far more challenges than that, you do not need the hardest ones — clear the easy and mid-tier challenges first and the trophy pops well before you run out. Check the menu after each stage of the roadmap and mop up the nearest ones.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.roadmap_note: Crime & money stage: 50 challenges complete — clear the easy ones first.

sources.name: GTABase — GTA 6 achievements & trophies list
Insider Gaming — Complete GTA 6 trophy list

Clear the easy and mid-tier challenges as you play through the stages.
The trophy pops when your fiftieth challenge completes.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: This trophy needs you and your partner to shake a four-star wanted level together and escape. Four stars means helicopters and a heavy police response, so set it up deliberately: build the wanted level with your partner beside you — robberies and shootouts raise it fastest — then break line of sight and drive for a hiding spot the police cannot see, such as a parking garage, a tunnel or dense back streets. Stay out of the search cones until the wanted level clears, and do not re-engage the police while hiding or the timer resets. The trophy pops when the wanted level drops to zero with your partner still with you. If your partner gets separated, regroup before you start the escape.
trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: easiest during a partner mission — lose a 4-star wanted level together.

Break line of sight and hide in a garage, tunnel or back streets.
Stay hidden until the wanted level clears; the trophy pops on escape.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: This trophy needs three shop robberies in a row, with your partner, without ever losing your wanted level between them. The key is the chain: you must keep the heat alive from the first robbery to the third, so plan a route of three shops close together and drive fast between them, never letting the wanted level drop. Keep your partner with you throughout, hit each shop quickly — get in, take the cash, get out — and do not stop to fight the police, since a long shootout wastes the window. A fast car parked outside each shop makes the chain much easier. The trophy pops when the third shop is robbed with the wanted level still active from the first.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: three shop robberies back-to-back with your partner, wanted level unbroken.

steps: Plan a route of three shops close together and keep a fast car ready.
With your partner, rob the first shop, then drive straight to the next without losing the wanted level.
Rob all three in one chain; the trophy pops on the third.

trophies.guide: Discovering a vehicle means encountering a new model — getting in it, or passing close enough for the game to register it — and this trophy needs 100 distinct vehicles. The count climbs naturally as you drive around Leonida, since every new car, bike, boat and aircraft you meet counts once. To finish it faster, vary your routes: city streets hold the common cars, the countryside and coast hold the trucks, bikes and boats, and the airport and docks hold the rarer machines. Steal or borrow anything unfamiliar rather than driving past it, and check the vehicle log in the stats screen to see how many you have found. The trophy pops at the hundredth distinct vehicle.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.roadmap_note: Collectibles stage: discover 100 distinct vehicles — vary your routes.

The trophy pops at the 100th distinct vehicle.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is the slow-motion aiming mode, and Gunslinger needs five takedowns inside a single use of it — one activation, five enemies down before it ends. The setup matters more than the aim: find a fight with at least five enemies grouped together, such as a gang shootout or a robbery escape, and activate Combat Focus only when they are all in view. Take them down one at a time with aimed headshots, and do not waste the slow time on cover or reloading — go in with a full magazine and a weapon you trust. If you only manage three or four, let the fight reset and try again in the next big shootout; there is no limit on attempts. Five takedowns in one Focus pops the trophy.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: five takedowns in one Combat Focus — best in a big shootout.

sources.name: GTABase — GTA 6 achievements & trophies list
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide & platinum roadmap

steps: Find a fight with five or more enemies grouped together.
Activate Combat Focus only when they are all in view, with a full magazine.
Take down five before the Focus ends; the trophy pops.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is Vice City International Airport, and this trophy is about leaving it in a way the airport did not schedule — stealing a plane and taking off without a flight plan, in other words. Head to the airport, get past the fences or the terminal onto the airfield, and take a plane: the trophy is about the departure itself, so get airborne and away from the airport. Expect a wanted level for trespassing and theft, so pick a fast plane, take off quickly, and lose the police in the air or by landing far from the airport. The name is a joke about unscheduled departures, and the trophy pops once you are airborne and clear. Try it in free roam if it does not come up during the VCIA Takedown mission.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: leave VCIA by an unscheduled departure — try it around the VCIA Takedown mission.

The trophy pops once you are airborne and clear of the airport.

trophies.guide: Rhinos are the tanks, and this trophy is about getting into one and surviving the heat that follows — the description's joke is that it gets hot inside a tank. Find a Rhino at a military base or wherever the army responds to high wanted levels, steal it, and take it for a drive: the trophy is about the tank itself, so getting in and moving with it is the core of it. Expect the full police and military response once you are in a tank, so drive it somewhere open, keep moving, and enjoy the armour while it lasts. The trophy pops once you have had your run in the Rhino. If tanks only appear at high wanted levels, build the heat first, then grab the Rhino when it arrives.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: get into a Rhino tank and take it for a run.

The trophy pops once you have taken the tank for a run.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: This trophy needs a clean jewelry store robbery: get in, take the goods and get out without any alarm or witness raising the alert. Stealth is the whole job, so plan it like a quiet job rather than a smash-and-grab: case the store first, watch the staff and camera positions, move when the floor is clear, and take the jewels without smashing cases in view of anyone. A suppressed approach and a quick exit matter more than speed inside the store, and if you are spotted, leave and try again — a failed attempt costs nothing but time. The trophy pops when you escape undetected with the loot. Do it in free roam when you can choose the quietest hour for the store.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.roadmap_note: Crime & money stage: rob a jewelry store clean, undetected.

trophies.guide: Bank vaults are the big robbery targets, and this silver trophy needs five of them robbed with a clean escape each time. Each vault is a planned job: case the bank, go in with a partner or a crew where the game allows it, crack or force the vault, grab the cash and get out before the police lock the area down. The escape is part of the requirement, so always have a fast getaway car parked close and a route out of the police search area planned before you go in. Five successful vault jobs pop the silver, and the money helps the economy trophies — laundering marked bills and spending in shops. Space the jobs out rather than rushing them back-to-back, since each one needs its own setup.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.roadmap_note: Crime & money stage: rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time.

Rob the vault, grab the cash and escape the police search area.
Repeat for five vaults; the silver pops on the fifth escape.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks drive the streets of Leonida carrying cash, and this trophy needs you to rob one and escape — a classic GTA set-piece, as the name says. Watch for a truck on the road, stop it by blocking it or forcing it off the road, then break into the back and take the cash. The guards will fight back and the police will respond, so the escape is the hard half: have a fast car ready, grab the money quickly, and break line of sight before the wanted level climbs. Trucks appear across the map, so you can attempt this whenever you spot one, and a failed attempt costs nothing — just find the next truck. The trophy pops when you escape with the cash.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.roadmap_note: Crime & money stage: rob an armored truck and escape.

Break into the back, take the cash and get to your getaway car.
Escape the police; the trophy pops when you are clear.

trophies.guide: Leonida is the whole state — Vice City, the coast, the swamps, the countryside and the small towns — and this trophy needs you to explore all of it. The game tracks which areas you have visited, so the work is systematic coverage: drive every region, visit every named place, and fill in the gaps on the map. The easiest method is to work region by region with the map open, marking off each area as you pass through it, and to fold in the other exploration trophies as you go — WAiNK It at 100 locations and discovering 100 vehicles both progress on the same trips. Check the map for unvisited corners and greyed-out areas, and finish them in the cleanup stage. The trophy pops when the last area is visited.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.roadmap_note: Collectibles stage: visit every area of Leonida, region by region.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Each gang in Leonida runs illegal operations — stash houses, labs, fronts — and this trophy needs you to rob one operation belonging to each gang. The work is finding them: each gang's territory holds its operations, so learn the map's gang areas, scout for the operation sites, and hit one per gang. You do not need to rob every operation, just one for each gang, so keep a list in this tracker of which gangs you have hit and which remain. Robberies raise your wanted level, so plan the escape for each hit as carefully as the hit itself. The trophy pops when the last gang's operation is robbed.

trophies.roadmap_note: Crime & money stage: rob one illegal operation per gang.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Ocean Beach is the Vice City beachfront, and this trophy is a quiet moment: have a cocktail somewhere with a view of it. Find a beachfront bar or a spot with a drink and a sea view, order the cocktail and let the scene play — the trophy is about the moment, not a challenge, so there is nothing to fail. It is the kind of trophy that is easy to walk past while chasing bigger objectives, so make a deliberate trip to Ocean Beach during the exploration stage, sit down with the view, and enjoy it. The trophy pops once the cocktail moment completes. Do it at sunset if you want the best view in the game.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: a quiet cocktail on Ocean Beach — do it when the story takes you there.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: This trophy is the classic GTA showroom smash: drive a car straight through a vehicle showroom's glass front and out the other side, in the style the series made famous. Pick a showroom with a big glass front, get a fast car, and drive through it at speed — the trophy is about the smash itself, so commit to it rather than slowing down at the glass. Expect a wanted level for the property damage, so have an escape route ready once you are through. It is a one-moment trophy, so set it up deliberately in free roam rather than hoping it happens by accident: choose the showroom, line up the run, and go. The trophy pops when you smash out.

trophies.roadmap_note: Story stage: smash a car through a vehicle showroom's glass front.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: The Kolt & Associates bowling alley is Leonida's bowling spot, and this trophy is about the follow-through — bowling a proper game there. Go to the alley, pick up a ball and play: the trophy centres on the bowling itself, so play a frame or a full game and let the follow-through animation and scoring play out. Bowling also counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None, so it does double duty. There is no score requirement mentioned in the description, so play naturally and enjoy the game; the trophy pops once the bowling moment completes. If you are already at the alley, play a full game — it is a relaxing break from the heists.

Hidden trophies like this one are story beats: they pop when the scene plays, and there is no separate task to complete. The honest advice is to play the story through and let it come — it is tied to a partnership moment, so it arrives in the course of the missions rather than in free roam. Because the description gives so little away, this guide does not invent a location or a step for it; the source lists confirm only that it is a hidden bronze tied to the story. Play the missions, and tick it off when it pops.

trophies.guide: This hidden trophy is about choices — decisions Lucia and Jason make in the story, for better or worse. Some story moments in GTA ask you to choose, and this trophy records that a choice was made, so the way to earn it is simply to reach the decision point in the story and pick a side. There is no wrong answer for the trophy itself: either choice counts, since the description is about the act of choosing rather than the outcome. The public lists confirm only that it is a hidden bronze tied to the story, so this guide does not invent a specific mission or outcome for it. Play the story, make the choice when it comes, and the trophy pops.

trophies.guide: This hidden trophy is about the second try — succeeding at something on a second attempt, as the description says. In practice that means a moment in the story or the open world where the first attempt fails and the retry succeeds, and the trophy pops on the successful second attempt. The public lists confirm only that it is a hidden bronze with that description, so this guide does not invent a specific event for it; the honest advice is to keep playing and, when something fails the first time, try it again rather than reloading an old save — the retry itself is what the trophy is about. It is one of the six hidden open-world secrets in the list, so it can come up anywhere in the game. Keep playing, retry what fails, and it will pop.

The public guides list it among the hidden open-world secrets, and its exact trigger is not something the lists spell out, so this guide does not invent one. The practical advice is to explore widely and pay attention: odd events, rare encounters and strange sights in the open world are what these secret trophies are built around, and this one rewards being in the right place at the right time. Keep exploring the map for The Goodtime State, visit unusual spots, and the moment will find you. The trophy pops when it happens.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by means striking someone from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon — a bat or similar — and this trophy needs you to bowl someone over that way. The setup is simple: get a melee weapon, find a vehicle with an open side or a bike, and drive past a target at speed, swinging as you pass. Bikes work well because you can swing freely, and a slow-moving target in an open area is easier to hit than someone in a crowd. The trophy is about the hit itself, so line up the pass, swing at the right moment, and keep driving — the police will notice, so have an escape in mind. It may take a few passes to land the timing; retry until the hit connects and the trophy pops.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are dirty money from robberies — bank vaults, armored trucks and gang operations all pay in them — and this trophy needs $250,000 of them laundered clean through your contacts. Laundering turns marked cash into spendable money, and your contacts are the people who do it, so the loop is: rob, collect marked bills, hand them to a contact, and repeat until the laundered total reaches $250,000. The number is cumulative, so every vault and truck job moves it forward, and the crime stage of this roadmap is designed to feed it. Keep robbing, keep laundering, and track the running total in the stats screen. The trophy pops when the laundered total hits $250,000.

trophies.guide: This trophy needs $100,000 spent across all shops — cumulative, in any shops, on anything. The simplest way to reach it is to spend as you play: weapons, ammo, armour, clothes, car mods and food all count, so do not hoard your money while the total sits uncounted. The crime stage pays well, and the money you launder for Dime on the Dollar is the same money you spend here, so the two trophies progress together. If you reach the endgame short of the total, the fastest way to close the gap is a big shopping run: upgrade your weapons, buy the expensive clothes and mod your favourite cars until the total passes $100,000. The trophy pops when the cumulative spend crosses the line.

trophies.guide: Garage properties are the buyable garages across Leonida where you store your vehicle collection, and this trophy needs all of them purchased. The public guides count eight garage properties, so the work is earning the money and then buying each one — the crime stage's robbery income is the natural funding for it. Garages appear for sale as you explore and progress, so check property listings regularly and buy each garage as soon as you can afford it rather than leaving them all for the endgame. Each garage also gives you somewhere to keep the vehicles you discover for Whip It Good, so the trophies support each other. The trophy pops when the last garage is bought.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app is the in-game service for registering vehicles, and this trophy needs ten vehicles registered through it. The loop is simple: find a vehicle, open the app, and register it — then repeat with nine more. Any vehicle you drive counts once it is registered, so fold this into Whip It Good: every new vehicle you discover is also a candidate for registration, and ten of them is a small number against the hundred you will find anyway. Use a mix of cars, bikes and anything else you come across, and the trophy pops on the tenth registration. It is one of the quickest trophies in the list if you register as you go.
